app.name: TensorFlow Quantum
app.one_liner: An open-source Python framework for hybrid quantum-classical machine learning that integrates Cirq-defined quantum circuits with TensorFlow’s scalable ML infrastructure.

screens.name: Quantum ML Workspace
screens.purpose: Enable users to define, simulate, and train hybrid quantum-classical models by combining Cirq circuits with TensorFlow constructs.
primary_actions: Compute gradients via parameter shift or adjoint methods

rust_commands.name: configure_keras_compatibility
rust_commands.purpose: Set environment variable TF_USE_LEGACY_KERAS=1 before importing TensorFlow or TensorFlow Quantum to ensure compatibility with Keras 2.

mvp_plan: week 1: Define a simple parameterized quantum circuit using Cirq
week 1: Embed circuit into a Keras model using TFQ layers
week 1: Install pinned versions of TensorFlow (2.18.1) and TensorFlow Quantum (0.7.6)
week 1: Set up environment with TF_USE_LEGACY_KERAS=1
week 1: Train model using parameter-shift gradient method
acceptance_tests: Application runs without error only when TF_USE_LEGACY_KERAS=1 is set before any TensorFlow import.
Framework supports Python 3.10–3.12 and NumPy 2 as stated in v0.7.6 release notes.
Quantum operations execute as first-class TensorFlow C++ ops within the compute graph.
